description:
From the fz-bdk diagnosis + user direction (2026-07-15): :bad + 1 is compile-time detectable -- the type layer already computes the empty return; the resolution is to CORRECT THE DATA: add @spec contracts to Kernel arithmetic in src/modules/runtime_library/kernel.fz (+ - * / div rem, unary minus; audit the operator family and neighbors like abs for the same gap), e.g. @spec +(number, number) :: number, so a demanded call site with non-number operands emits the FATAL spec-violation diagnostic through the machinery landed in fz-9i4.7.1.3 (fixtures spec_violation/spec_mixed_protocol_concrete_violation show the pattern; Map @specs show the library convention). PARITY BY CONSTRUCTION: a compile diagnostic cannot diverge across run/interp/build.

RE-PIN the affected surfaces: fixtures2/behavior/opaque_fn_all_divergent becomes a compile-diagnostic fixture (all legs expect the spec-violation error -- honest red becomes honest compile error); the drive_test that pins halt_value=function_clause via JIT (compiler2_all_divergent_public_callable_has_no_result_continuation) re-pinned to the new contract; promote the fz-bdk spike p7 fixture (branch wt/bdk-spike @ 99071ece8, fixtures2/spikes/fz-bdk/) as a compile-diagnostic fixture too. SWEEP: verify no legitimate corpus/library code trips the new specs (Enum/List internals use arithmetic on numbers -- should be clean; any trip is a real finding). NOTE the strictness choice: statically-doomed code in an untaken branch becomes a compile ERROR (fz spec violations are fatal, stricter than Elixir warn) -- consistent with the 9i4.7.1.3 contract.

comments.text:
PREMISE REFUTED (2026-07-15, correct STOP, nothing committed, worktree clean). (1) Kernel arithmetic ALREADY carries precise @specs (landed fz-0fb/196dbbc29 before this ticket): integer+integer::integer, float+float::float, mixed arrows -- every concrete overload of + - * / % is specced; div/rem/abs do not exist in the library. THERE IS NO DATA GAP. (2) The landed spec machinery structurally CANNOT fire for Kernel calls: function_contract_is_enforced (jobs/semantic.rs:1580-1583) exempts ALL bootstrap-defined code (is_bootstrap = Kernel/Enum/Map/List..., world.rs:1202) -- introduced by the same commit that landed the machinery (e1ecccd8e). (3) CAUSALITY PROVEN: removing the gate makes dbg(:bad + 1) produce exactly the desired error[spec/violation]: call to +/2 violates its @spec for arguments (:bad, int) -- AND breaks 74 lib tests (enum_reduce_operator_refs / transport_contract / port_* -- internal Enum machinery routing operator REFS through Kernel with erased types). Blanket removal unsafe. (4) Unary minus CANNOT be specced: UnOp::Neg lowers to ExprStep::UnaryOp (body.rs:1726-1731), no call path, lowered_unop_ty falls back to any -- needs a code-shape change, separate concern.

DECISION NEEDED (policy/architecture): how to enforce bootstrap-callee specs without false-firing on the library's own generic/erased internal calls. Options: (a) CALLER-KEYED -- enforce when the caller is non-bootstrap user code; internal machinery stays exempt; risk = user code passing legitimately-any values might false-fatal depending on the checker's comparison semantics. (b) DISJOINTNESS-ONLY for bootstrap callees -- violation fires only when the argument type is PROVABLY DISJOINT from the spec domain (atom vs number); any/erased passes; likely also un-breaks the 74 (their args are erased, not disjoint); the sound gradual-typing notion. (c) both. Ticket paused pending direction.

title: spec Kernel arithmetic (+/2 and friends): ill-typed operands become fatal compile-time spec violations through the landed contract machinery
